headlines.title: Why Chevron Investors Could Make Sense Of ETFs Now
headlines.summary: You might like Chevron for its global energy reach, but owning the stock directly means carrying its specific risks by yourself. Simply Wall St highlights one of those: that earnings are forecast to decline an average of 5.2% per year over the next 3 years. Holding Chevron through a fund that also owns other businesses spreads how much those company specific issues can swing your portfolio, and also spreads out how much its success can help you. Right now the story has fresh twists.

headlines.summary: ETFs sold $65.9 million of Chevron (CVX) on Monday, with 24 sellers against 38 buyers.

headlines.title: Earnings Surge Could Be A Game Changer For Chevron Stock (CVX)
headlines.summary: Chevron reported third quarter earnings of US$9.9b, with nearly triple profit versus a year earlier, supported by record U.S. refinery throughput, stronger refining margins, lower debt and new upstream exposure in Venezuela and offshore Greece. The dividend currently appears covered at about US$65 Brent per barrel. Cash generation from refining and upstream operations remains central to how Chevron funds shareholder distributions while ETFs have recently been net sellers.

headlines.summary: Tributary Capital Management released its Q3 2026 investor letter, titled “All Cap Equity Strategy”. A copy of the letter can be downloaded here. description: Chevron Corporation, through its subsidiaries, engages in the integrated energy and chemicals operations. It operates through Upstream and Downstream segments. The Upstream segment engages in the exploration for, development, production, and transportation of crude oil and natural gas; processing, liquefaction, transportation, and regasification of liquefied natural gas; transportation of crude oil through pipelines; transportation, storage, and marketing of natural gas; carbon capture and storage; and operation of a gas-to-liquids plant. The Downstream segment refines crude oil into petroleum products; markets crude oil, refined products, and lubricants; manufactures and markets renewable fuels; transports crude oil and refined products through pipeline, marine vessel, motor equipment, and rail car; and manufactures and markets commodity petrochemicals, plastics for industrial uses, and fuel and lubricant additives. The company operates in North America, South America, Europe, Africa, Asia, and Australia. The company was formerly known as ChevronTexaco Corporation and changed its name to Chevron Corporation in May 2005. Chevron Corporation was founded in 1879 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas.
